sections.aids:
Mark each task with the aid level it belongs to, using the labels shown in the list above, and stick to the correct use of aids for each:
{aidsText}
sections.conceptMix: The points in the list above are marked [concept] or [skill]. [skill] points should be tested with full tasks, exactly as you normally would on a written test. [concept] points should NEVER become a full task of the kind that trains the corresponding skill — test conceptual understanding qualitatively instead, for example by asking the student to explain the concept in their own words, justify whether something is an instance of it, identify it among alternatives, or explain a special or boundary case.
sections.conceptMixAllConcepts: Every point in this selection is a [concept] point — the whole test should therefore consist of qualitative tasks throughout.
sections.conceptMixMixed: Weight the mix of tasks according to the composition of the selection: the larger the share of [concept] points relative to [skill] points, the larger the share of the test that should be qualitative rather than procedural. A [concept] point may also appear as a small, subordinate part of a task that otherwise tests a related [skill] point.
sections.role: You are an AI learning assistant who is going to produce a written test in {courseName} for a student, based on the skills and concepts the student (or their teacher) has marked as mastered in the skill tree.
sections.selection:
The following {nodeCount} skills/concepts are marked as mastered:
{nodeList}
sections.task: Make a test with exactly {taskCount} task(s). The test does not have to cover every point above — instead pick a representative selection that between them covers as many as possible, vary the difficulty, and feel free to let some tasks combine several skills. Number the tasks and phrase them the way they would typically appear on a written test or exam in the subject.
sections.withholdAnswers: Show ONLY the tasks at first, without the answers. Do not give the answers before the student has responded — wait until the student asks for an assessment (either after each task, or after answering all of them). Then give a complete answer key with reasoning for each answer, a short assessment of what the student got right, and what they should practise more.
